records.s: The Forest of Burzee is a vast, ancient forest with closely packed trees, dense foliage, mosses, lichens, and dried leaves. It is described as mighty, grand, and filled with peaceful natural sounds and changing shadows. Nature originally populated Burzee with Fairies, Knooks, Ryls, and Nymphs, who live there as sweet immortals. Civilization has never reached the forest, though it is uncertain whether it ever will.

records.l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, YOUTH / 1. Burzee
records.s: The Forest of Burzee is a mighty, grand, and ancient forest whose trees have intertwined roots and branches. It provides a home, refuge, and playground for its inhabitants and remains largely untouched by civilization.

records.l: inhabitants of Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, YOUTH / 1. Burzee
records.s: The inhabitants of Burzee are Fairies, Knooks, Ryls, and Nymphs, who were placed there by Nature. They are sweet immortals who live, revel, and play undisturbed in the forest's depths.

records.l: Civilization, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, YOUTH / 1. Burzee
records.s: Civilization has never reached the Forest of Burzee. Whether it will ever reach the forest remains uncertain.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
records.s: Necile, a wood-nymph of the Forest of Burzee, becomes restless with her uneventful duties and longs for meaningful adventure. Ak tells the nymphs that he found a human infant abandoned near the forest and ordered the lioness Shiegra to protect it and feed it. Defying the Law of the Forest, Necile leaves the forest’s depths, finds the sleeping infant, and carries it away into the forest after it reaches for her.

records.l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
records.s: Necile is a beautiful wood-nymph related to Queen Zurline who guards trees in the Forest of Burzee. As her duties become easier and less frequent, she grows discontented and longs for adventure. After hearing about a human infant in danger, she breaks the Law of the Forest, finds the child, and carries it into the forest.

records.l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
records.s: The Forest of Burzee is a great forest inhabited by wood-nymphs and governed by the Law of the Forest. Its trees have become old and sturdy, and weeds and Gadgols no longer threaten them as they once did.

records.l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
records.s: Ak is the Master Woodsman of the world and is said to see everything and know more than the sons of men. He sometimes rescues helpless human children from misery, including four children saved from freezing and a newborn infant threatened by a lioness. He orders Shiegra to protect the infant and give it milk until he can attend to other matters.

records.l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
records.s: The wood-nymphs guard forests, minister to young trees, and dress in oak-leaf green. They participate in festivals and dances, listen to Ak’s words of wisdom, and are generally sheltered within the inner parts of the Forest of Burzee by its law.

records.l: Law of the Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
records.s: The Law of the Forest restrains wood-nymphs from leaving the forest in search of adventure. Necile knowingly breaks this law when she goes to find the human infant.

records.l: Shiegra, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
records.s: Shiegra is a lioness who crouches near the Forest of Burzee, intending to devour the abandoned human infant. Ak commands her to lie beside the infant, feed it her milk, and ensure that no beast or reptile harms it.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. The Child of the Forest
records.s: The human infant is found newborn, naked, helpless, and crying on the grass near the Forest of Burzee. Shiegra quiets its hunger with her milk under Ak’s command, after which the infant sleeps, smiles at Necile, reaches toward her, and is carried into the forest by her.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
records.s: Ak, the Master Woodsman, discovers that Necile has brought a sleeping human infant into the Forest of Burzee. Necile asks to keep and care for the infant, arguing that Ak can permit her to do so. Ak agrees to the adoption and grants the infant his protection, but declares that no mortal will ever again be adopted by an immortal. Necile rejoices and takes the infant to her bower.

records.l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
records.s: Ak discovers Necile holding the sleeping infant and recognizes that she has defied his Law. He permits Necile to keep the infant and promises to protect it, while declaring that this is the final time he will relax the Law.

records.l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
records.s: Necile brings the sleeping infant into the Forest of Burzee and asks Ak to let her keep and care for it. After Ak grants her request, she hurries to her bower to rejoice over her new-found treasure.

records.l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
records.s: The nymphs are surprised and dismayed to see Necile standing with the infant. They hear Ak permit Necile to keep the child, and Queen Zurline encourages Ak to grant the petition.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
records.s: The infant is sleeping, weak, and helpless when Necile presents it to Ak and the nymphs. Ak allows Necile to keep it and gives it his protection.

records.l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
records.s: The Forest of Burzee is the place where Necile wants to raise the infant, although the human race has never penetrated it. Necile considers it her home and believes the infant cannot harm it.

records.l: the Law, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. The Adoption
records.s: The Law forbids an immortal from adopting a mortal. Ak relaxes the Law to allow Necile to keep the infant, but declares that it will never again be relaxed for this purpose.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
records.s: Necile and the forest nymphs care for the human infant, naming him Claus or Neclaus after the Queen suggests the name. Claus grows up in Necile's bower, fed by milk from bell-udders, does, and Shiegra, while Necile teaches him to speak, walk, and play. Ak's decree protects Claus from the beasts, and the Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies visit him and become fond of him. Claus learns their laws and believes the Forest of Burzee is the whole world, unaware that other human beings exist.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
records.s: Claus is raised by Necile and the forest nymphs in Necile's bower, where he grows big and sturdy. He is gentle, fearless, playful, and loved by the Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies; he learns their laws and believes the forest is the entire world.

records.l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
records.s: Necile names the infant Claus, gathers soft moss for his bed, and cares for him in her bower. She teaches him to speak, walk, and play, and loves to call him Claus even after the Queen suggests the name Neclaus.

records.l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
records.s: Ak sanctions the nymphs' adoption of the human infant. His decree forbids beasts and reptiles from molesting Claus, allowing him to walk fearlessly through the forest.

records.l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
records.s: The forest nymphs gather around Claus with curiosity and delight and praise Ak for allowing Necile to keep him. They search for bell-udders to provide him with milk and help care for him as he grows.

records.l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
records.s: The Forest of Burzee is where Claus is raised and where the nymphs, Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies visit him. Claus comes to regard it as the whole world because he does not know that other human beings exist.

records.l: Claus's adoption by Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. Claus
records.s: The adoption of Claus by Necile and the forest nymphs is sanctioned by Ak. It attracts the interest of the Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies, whose customs or laws had not prepared them for an immortal community adopting a human child.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
records.s: Claus grows from infancy to a stalwart youth while living among Necile and the immortals of Burzee. He learns the language and lore of the forest and helps the Ryls and Knooks with their work. When Ak returns to Burzee, he observes Claus closely and decides to take him on a journey through the world. Necile grieves at the separation and clings to Claus as Ak watches them thoughtfully.

records.l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
records.s: Burzee remains a vast forest inhabited by nymphs, Ryls, Knooks, and many animals. Claus explores its heart, learns its natural lore, and helps maintain its plants and animals.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
records.s: Claus grows to manhood, becoming a broad-shouldered and stalwart youth. He learns the language of the beasts, the songs of the bees, the poetry of the wood-flowers, and the history of Burzee's owls, while helping the Ryls and Knooks. Ak later asks him to accompany him on a journey through the world.

records.l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
records.s: Necile raises Claus and comes to love him dearly. She adapts her life to follow him through Burzee and teaches him about the forest and its inhabitants. She weeps when Ak takes Claus away for a time and clings to him as if she cannot bear to let him go.

records.l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
records.s: Ak returns to Burzee after visiting his many forests throughout the world. He studies Claus's face and is relieved to find his eyes placid and his heart brave and innocent. He calls Claus aside and tells him to accompany him on a journey through the world.

records.l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
records.s: The nymphs remain immortal and unchanging while Claus grows from a child into a youth. They follow Claus through the forest paths, explain Burzee's mysteries and living creatures to him, and protect and favor him along with Queen Zurline.

records.l: journey through the world, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. The Master Woodsman
records.s: Ak plans for Claus to accompany him on a journey through the world after Ak has visited his many forests. Claus is pleased by the honor, while Necile is distressed by his departure.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
records.s: Ak takes Claus on a journey around the world so he can see the many human beings from whom he is descended. Claus learns that humanity is numerous, unequal in wealth and circumstances, and subject to mortality, while the immortals are few. He becomes especially interested in the children and longs to help them, remembering how Necile rescued him as a baby. When Claus returns to the Forest of Burzee, he is thoughtful and no longer as carefree as before.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
records.s: Claus travels with Ak through the air and visits many human settlements while remaining invisible by holding the Master's girdle. He learns that he is descended from humanity and that he was abandoned at the forest's edge before Necile rescued him. After seeing the lives of people and children, he longs to become helpful to his fellows and returns to Burzee grave and thoughtful.

records.l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
records.s: Ak takes Claus around the world to show him the haunts and lives of human beings. He explains the differences between mortals and immortals, the unequal conditions of children, Claus's babyhood, and the purpose of helpful lives. He returns Claus safely to the Forest of Burzee.

records.l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
records.s: Necile had rescued Claus when he was abandoned at the edge of the forest and had brought him to manhood under the protection of the immortals. She anxiously awaits his return and sighs when she sees how deeply thoughtful he has become.

records.l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
records.s: The Forest of Burzee is Claus's home, where he was reared among the immortals after Necile rescued him. Ak and Claus return there after traveling around the world, and Claus is set down among the circle of nymphs.

records.l: humanity, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
records.s: Humanity is numerous and includes people with many different natures, conditions, and occupations. Mortals must struggle and worry for wealth, eventually perish, and are born in both cottages and palaces. Ak teaches that helpful people are sure to live again.

records.l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
records.s: Claus observes children living in poverty and wealth, including ragged children playing in dust and richly dressed children fed with sugar-plums. He sees them as equally fair and sweet and believes childhood is the time of greatest content, before the cares of humanity overtake them. Their condition awakens his love, pity, and desire to help.

records.l: journey through the world, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. Claus Discovers Humanity
records.s: Ak's journey around the world with Claus begins in a clearing in the Forest of Burzee and carries them through the air to cities and dwellings in many parts of the earth. They observe farmers, warriors, merchants, and children before returning to Burzee. The journey changes Claus from an ever-joyous boy into a grave and thoughtful youth.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: Claus tells Queen Zurline and the Forest people that, as a son of humanity, he must leave the Forest and accept the brief, difficult life of mankind. He chooses to devote himself to caring for the children of mankind, hoping to make them happy as Necile made him happy. Ak grants Claus continued protection and the assistance of the Nymphs, Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies. Claus leaves Burzee and chooses the Laughing Valley of Hohaho as his home.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: Claus recognizes that he belongs to humanity and decides to leave the Forest to live according to mankind's lot. He chooses to devote his life to making children happy, and Ak grants him continued protection and the aid of the Forest people.

records.l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: Necile is remembered by Claus as his loving foster-mother and comrade. Claus kisses her and promises to love and cherish her while he lives, while she silently embraces and kisses him tenderly at his departure.

records.l: Master Woodsman, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: Ak confirms that Claus has spoken well and declares that Claus will retain the Forest's protection and his existing powers after entering the world of men. Ak also promises that the Nymphs, Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies will serve Claus when he calls upon them, and he guides Claus's steps after he leaves.

records.l: Nymphs, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: The nymphs listen as Claus explains why he must leave them and proudly promise to give him their sympathy and help. They remain among the Forest people whose aid Ak grants Claus.

records.l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: Burzee remains the Forest that Claus leaves when he begins his life among men. Claus passes through Burzee to reach its eastern edge and the Laughing Valley of Hohaho.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: The Laughing Valley of Hohaho lies at the eastern edge of Burzee, between green hills with a brook running through it. Its cheerful natural life restores Claus's merriment, and he chooses the valley as his home.

records.l: humanity, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: Humanity is described as living briefly, working for its needs, growing old, and dying, while each person has a mission to leave the world better than they found it. Claus accepts humanity's lot as his own and leaves the Forest to take his part in its struggle.

records.l: Claus's departure from the Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: Claus says farewell to the Forest people by turning away rather than speaking a formal goodbye, because his wild Forest life is over. He then passes through Burzee and goes out toward the world of men.

records.l: Santa Claus's mission to bring happiness to children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. Claus Leaves the Forest
records.s: Claus decides to care for the children of mankind and devote his life to their pleasure. He hopes that Necile's kindness in adopting and caring for him will be remembered through the happiness he brings to thousands of children.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus settles in the Laughing Valley and begins building a home without harming living trees or flowers. The Knooks build his house, while the Fairies provide household tools, food-preparation items, clothing, blankets, and other comforts. The Spirit of Happiness removes Claus's fears and cares, and the Ryls of the Field Flowers promise to supply his food so he will not need to cultivate the flower-filled ground. Claus therefore begins a peaceful life supported by the immortals.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus comes to the empty Laughing Valley, builds a house from fallen trees, and chooses not to cut living trees or destroy flowers. He receives help and supplies from the Knooks, Fairies, and Ryls of the Field Flowers, and begins a happy life devoted to doing good.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The Laughing Valley is a peaceful, flower-filled place inhabited by grass, a brook, wildflowers, bees, and butterflies. It claims Claus as its tenant, brings him happiness, and becomes his home.

records.l: Master Woodsman, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The Master Woodsman sends his servant Nelko with a strong, bright ax for Claus. He also sends the Fairies to provide Claus with household supplies and clothing.

records.l: immortals, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The immortals appear to have directed Claus's steps toward the Laughing Valley after he left Burzee. The Knooks, Fairies, Ryls, and other friendly beings support him there.

records.l: Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The Forest has taught Claus that living trees are sacred and endowed with feeling. Claus applies this lesson by using only fallen trees for his house.

records.l: house (Claus's house), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus's house is built during the night by the Knooks from logs he has prepared. It has a large room with a fireplace, table, bench, and cupboard, along with a smaller room containing a bed, stool, stand, and dried moss.

records.l: Spirit of Happiness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The Spirit of Happiness enters Claus's heart while he sleeps in the Valley. It drives out his terror, care, and misgivings so that he will no longer be clouded by anxiety.

records.l: brook, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The brook provides Claus with pure drinking water. Its ripples playfully race and sing as they move through the Valley.

records.l: Knooks, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The Knooks silently and skillfully build Claus's house while he sleeps. They later cut and stack wood for his fireplace, and Claus thanks them for their work and knowledge of human needs.

records.l: Fairies, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The Fairies bring Claus skillets, pots, dishes, pans, cooking tools, wool clothing, and other comforts. They also provide warm blankets and clothing as his life in the Valley begins.

records.l: Ryls, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The Ryls of the Field Flowers promise to supply Claus with food so that he will not need to plow the ground and destroy the flowers and grass. They subsequently provide milk, bread, honey, apples, grapes, and continuing food supplies.

records.l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: Ak has spoken to the Ryls of the Field Flowers about Claus. Although Ak has no command over the field Ryls because he is not of the Forest, they are willing to favor Claus because Ak loves him.

records.l: field flowers, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The field flowers grow throughout the Valley and are tended by the Ryls of the Field Flowers. Claus refuses to destroy them by plowing the earth and values their songs and beauty.

records.l: food supplies, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: The Ryls of the Field Flowers provide Claus with food supplies so he will not have to cultivate the ground. These supplies include fresh milk, bread, honey, apples, and grapes, and they remain available whenever he is hungry.

records.l: Happiness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: Happiness fills the Laughing Valley and is expressed by the brook, daffodils, sunbeams, and other living things. Claus recognizes the Valley as a place of happiness, joy, peace, and good-will.

records.l: Claus's life in the Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, MANHOOD / 1. The Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus's life in the Laughing Valley begins with the favor and friendship of the immortals. His house, food, clothing, firewood, and other needs are supplied, allowing him to live peacefully while preparing to do good work.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. How Claus Made the First Toy
records.s: Claus befriends children throughout the countryside and brings comfort and happiness to those who welcome him, though he is refused entry to the palace of the Lord of Lerd and the castle of Baron Braun. When winter arrives, Claus worries that the cold and snow will keep him from seeing the children. While indoors, he carves a wooden cat modeled after Blinkie, creating his first toy. Blinkie's reactions amuse Claus and confirm his pleasure in the finished work.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. How Claus Made the First Toy
records.s: Claus travels through the Valley and the surrounding plain to visit villages and befriend children. He comforts poor, abused, crippled, ailing, and grieving people, but he is refused admission to the palace of the Lord of Lerd and the castle of Baron Braun. During the winter, he carves a wooden cat from a stick of wood and makes his first toy.

records.l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. How Claus Made the First Toy
records.s: Children in the villages welcome Claus as a playfellow, riding on his shoulders, nesting in his arms, and clinging to his knees. They have been much neglected by their parents, so Claus's attention makes them very happy. Claus worries that winter will prevent him from seeing them.

records.l: Jack Frost, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. How Claus Made the First Toy
records.s: Jack Frost visits Claus at night and boasts that he will nip many noses, ears, and toes. After Claus asks him to spare the children because they are tender and helpless, Jack promises not to pinch a child that night if he can resist the temptation.

records.l: Blinkie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. How Claus Made the First Toy
records.s: Blinkie is a large cat given to Claus by Peter the Knook, and she sits beside the hearth while Claus stays indoors. She watches Claus carve a wooden cat, first reacting angrily to the image and then recognizing that it is made of wood. She resumes purring and gives Claus admiring glances.

records.l: toy cat, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. How Claus Made the First Toy
records.s: The first toy is a wooden cat that Claus carves from a stick of firewood during a long winter evening. He shapes it with a cat's head, body, haunches, tail, ears, eyes, and nose, modeling it after Blinkie. The completed toy pleases Claus and amuses him when Blinkie reacts to it.

records.l: winter, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. How Claus Made the First Toy
records.s: Winter approaches after the flowers, beetles, butterflies, and brook have changed with the season. Snow covers the Laughing Valley, and the cold keeps Claus indoors for many days. During this period, Claus grows weary of having little to do and begins carving wood.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. How Claus Made the First Toy
records.s: The Laughing Valley is where Claus lives and where snowflakes fall heavily when winter arrives. Its winter weather covers Claus's dwelling in white and makes it difficult for him to visit the children.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: Claus rescues Weekum from a snowdrift during a storm and gives him a wooden cat to keep. The Ryls help Claus color a second wooden cat to resemble a real cat, and the toy brings comfort to a sick girl. Inspired by Shiegra, Claus then carves and paints a wooden lioness. These events begin Claus's great work of making toys for children.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: Claus rescues Weekum from a snowdrift, warms and feeds him, and carries him home to his mother. He makes and colors wooden cats with help from the Ryls, gives one to a sick girl, and then carves and paints a wooden lioness after Shiegra's suggestion.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: The Laughing Valley is covered in snow during a fierce winter storm. Claus lives there, and after the wind moves north and the snow settles, he travels through the Valley to help others.

records.l: Blinkie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: Blinkie is Claus's real cat. She hides under the table when the wind blows into the house, sits as a model while Claus paints the toy cat, appears offended by the attention given to it, and later becomes terrified when Shiegra snarls at her.

records.l: toy cat, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: The toy cat is a wooden imitation of a real cat. Weekum likes it because it does not run away, scratch, or bite, and a colored toy cat later comforts a sick girl by easing her fever and pain.

records.l: Weekum, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: Weekum is a little boy who becomes lost while walking to his auntie's house during a snowstorm. Claus finds and cares for him, and Weekum receives the wooden cat and takes it home to his mother.

records.l: Ryls, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: The Red, Green, Yellow, Black, and Blue Ryls visit Claus while he is carving a wooden cat. They bring paints and brushes made from the colors they use on flowers and plants, then help color the cat to resemble a real one.

records.l: colored toy-making, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: Claus begins making better wooden cats after deciding children will enjoy toys that cannot scratch or bite. With the Ryls' paints, he colors the cats' features and body to imitate real cats, beginning his great work of making toys.

records.l: sick girl, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: A sick girl lies on a wretched cot in a poor hut near the palace of the Lord of Lerd. Claus gives her a colored wooden cat, which brings her pleasure, quiets her fever, lessens her pain, and helps her fall asleep.

records.l: Shiegra, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: Shiegra is an old lioness who has loved Claus since his babyhood and visits him in the Laughing Valley despite her dislike of snow-drifts. She suggests that Claus make a lioness toy, admires the finished likeness, and returns toward her forest home after snarling at Blinkie.

records.l: wooden lioness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: Claus carves a wooden lioness in Shiegra's likeness, including her fierce teeth, frowning lines, crouching body, and long tail. He paints it with the Ryls' colors, and Shiegra considers it skillfully made and likely to please children.

records.l: rescue of Weekum, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 3. How the Ryls Colored the Toys
records.s: During a snowstorm, Claus hears a cry of distress and finds Weekum buried in a snowdrift. He carries the child into his house, warms and feeds him, lets him sleep with the wooden cat, and returns him safely to his mother the next morning.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: In spring, Mayrie and her younger brother visit Claus in the Laughing Valley to ask for toy cats. When Claus shows Mayrie an image of the lioness Shiegra, both children become frightened and flee. Claus makes Mayrie a wooden cat and decides to model future toys on mild animals instead of fierce creatures. His toys become popular, and the immortals help supply him with wood, paints, brushes, and tools.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: After winter ends, the Laughing Valley becomes filled with joyous excitement, with the brook, grass, sun, and other natural features seeming lively and happy. Claus says that living in the Laughing Valley, where everything else laughs, makes him sing, laugh, and whistle.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Claus welcomes Mayrie and her younger brother, feeds them, and gives the boy his last ready-made toy cat. After frightening Mayrie with Shiegra's image, he makes her a wooden cat and decides to use mild animals as models for future toys. His toy-making becomes so popular that he turns his living room into a workshop, while the Knooks, Ryls, and Fairies supply materials and tools.

records.l: Mayrie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Mayrie visits Claus with her younger brother because she wants a toy cat. She cries when Claus gives the only ready cat to her brother, becomes terrified by Shiegra's image, and later happily watches Claus carve and paint a cat for her.

records.l: Mayrie's younger brother, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Mayrie's younger brother accompanies her to Claus's house and echoes her request for a cat. He receives Claus's last ready-made toy cat but drops it while fleeing in fear from Shiegra's image.

records.l: Shiegra, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Shiegra is the lioness known to Claus, who is familiar with her and is not afraid of her. Claus realizes that children may view her as terrifying rather than friendly.

records.l: Shiegra's image, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Claus takes the image of Shiegra from his cupboard and offers it to Mayrie as a toy. Its fierce teeth and glaring eyes frighten both children, so Claus locks it back in the cupboard and decides not to use fierce creatures as toy models.

records.l: toy cats, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Claus's toy cats are popular with children. He gives one to Mayrie's younger brother, carries two to children in town, and later carves and paints another cat for Mayrie.

records.l: toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Claus's toy animals spread in fame to cottages on the plain and in the village, and no child who visits him goes away empty-handed. After Mayrie's reaction, he chooses squirrels, rabbits, deer, and lambkins as gentler models, and begins making wooden rabbits and lambs.

records.l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Children travel to Claus's house to obtain his wonderful toys, while Claus carries gifts to children who are sick or crippled. Their visits create a path from the plain to his cottage, and their pleasure makes Claus happy.

records.l: colored toy-making, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Claus's toy-making grows from carving cats into a larger enterprise producing rabbits, lambs, and other animal figures. The Knooks provide wood, the Ryls provide paints and brushes, and the Fairies bring tools, allowing Claus to work continuously in his workshop.

records.l: Mayrie's fright, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 4. How Little Mayrie Became Frightened
records.s: Mayrie's fright begins when she sees the fierce teeth and glaring eyes of Shiegra's image. Her terror causes her and her brother to flee, and it teaches Claus that children's toys should be mild and pleasant rather than fierce.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus gives in to Bessie Blithesome’s request for a toy and seeks advice from Necile and the Queen of the Fairies about whether rich children should receive his toys. The Queen declares that all children’s wishes and sufferings matter equally, so Claus decides to make toys for rich and poor alike. Claus creates the first dolly from clay in the likeness of Necile, then makes a baby dolly and a dressed image of Bessie. He gives the Bessie image dolly to Mayrie after she breaks her toy cat, making her very happy.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus promises Bessie Blithesome that he will make her a toy, then consults Necile and the Queen of the Fairies about whether he should give toys to rich children. He creates several clay dolls, including a toy nymph and an image of Bessie, and gives the Bessie image dolly to Mayrie.

records.l: Bessie Blithesome, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Bessie Blithesome visits Claus with an escort of men-at-arms and asks for a toy, explaining that she has none despite being a rich lord’s daughter. Claus gives her a clay nymph doll, which she loves and calls her baby.

records.l: Mayrie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Mayrie comes to Claus crying because she has broken her toy cat by dropping it twice. Claus gives her the silk-robed Bessie image dolly, and Mayrie receives it with great joy.

records.l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Necile listens to Claus’s concern about giving toys to rich children and says that riches are only like a gown that can be put on or removed, while children remain alike. Claus makes the first toy nymph in her likeness.

records.l: Queen Zurline, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: The Queen of the Fairies tells Claus that rich and poor children alike naturally long for pretty playthings and can suffer loneliness or enjoy happiness. She declares that it is his duty to make all children glad.

records.l: Fairies, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: The Fairies help Claus make the Bessie image dolly by bringing colored silks, laces, and golden threads for its clothing.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: The Laughing Valley is where Claus lives and where Bessie’s cavalcade arrives at his dwelling. After consulting Necile and the Queen of the Fairies, Claus returns to the Valley to make dolls.

records.l: toy nymph, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus forms the toy nymph from moist clay, bakes it in the sun until it becomes hard, and paints it to resemble Necile. He gives it to Bessie, who loves it and calls it a dolly.

records.l: Bessie image dolly, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus makes the Bessie image dolly from clay, bakes it over glowing coals, and dresses it in a lavender silk gown, lace collar, and pink silk shoes. He paints its face with Bessie’s brown eyes, golden hair, and rosy cheeks before giving it to Mayrie.

records.l: toy, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Bessie asks Claus for a toy because there are no toys in the world but his. Claus first promises her the next toy he makes, and the toy nymph becomes the gift that delights her.

records.l: riches, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus initially thinks riches provide enough comforts that rich children should not need his toys. Necile explains that riches are like a removable gown and do not change the child beneath them.

records.l: children's happiness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: The Queen of the Fairies teaches Claus that rich children can be as lonely, unhappy, gay, and happy as poor children. Children’s happiness therefore should not depend on whether they live in palaces or cottages.

records.l: Claus's decision to make toys for all children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: After hearing Necile and the Queen of the Fairies, Claus decides that all children may claim his services, whether they are rich or poor. He then begins making toys for Bessie as well as for poor children.

records.l: creation of the first dolly, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: Claus unintentionally shapes moist clay into a head resembling Necile, then develops it into a toy nymph with hair, an oak-leaf gown, sandals, painted eyes, teeth, lips, and hair. The baked and painted figure becomes the first dolly, which he gives to Bessie.

records.l: Mayrie receiving the dolly, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 5. How Bessie Blithesome Came to the Laughing Valley
records.s: When Mayrie’s toy cat is broken, Claus offers her the silk-robed Bessie image dolly instead. Mayrie loves the beautiful figure and carries it home happily, saying it is better than cats.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The Awgwas are invisible, evil creatures who influence people toward wickedness and decide to destroy Claus because his toys make children happier and more obedient. They abduct Claus to a jungle in Ethop and later imprison him in a mountain cave, but the Knooks and Fairies rescue him, while Queen Zurline and other immortals protect his home. The Awgwas then steal Claus's toys and prevent children from reaching the Laughing Valley, causing Claus to stop traveling and fill his home with toys. Finally, Claus asks the great Ak for help against the Awgwas' persecution.

records.l: Awgwas, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The Awgwas are gigantic, evil creatures who are invisible to ordinary people but visible to immortals. They influence human minds, delight in wicked deeds, fight among themselves, and use their powers to attack Claus and prevent him from bringing happiness to children.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: Claus makes toys to bring happiness to children and thereby keeps them from the Awgwas' influence. After being abducted and repeatedly attacked, he continues making toys, but eventually asks the great Ak for help when the Awgwas prevent him from delivering them.

records.l: King Awgwa, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The King Awgwa proposes destroying Claus because Claus's toys have made children less naughty and less vulnerable to the Awgwas. He orders attempts to abduct, imprison, and rob Claus, but each effort to destroy or permanently confine him fails.

records.l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The children are influenced by the Awgwas to quarrel, disobey, and behave badly, but Claus's toys make them happier and more obedient. The Awgwas prevent them from finding the Laughing Valley after Claus stops traveling to the villages.

records.l: Knooks, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The Knooks of the Forest rescue Claus after the Awgwas leave him bound in the jungle of Ethop. Recognizing the secret sign and signal of their order, they free him, give him food and drink, and transport him back to the Laughing Valley.

records.l: Queen Zurline, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: Queen Zurline learns of Claus's persecution and declares that the immortals must protect him. She places her Seal on every door and window of Claus's dwelling, adding it to the Seals of the Fairies, Ryls, and Knooks.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The Laughing Valley is Claus's home and the place where he makes his toys. The Awgwas prevent children from reaching it after Claus gives up trying to travel to the villages.

records.l: immortals, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The immortals fear and avoid the Awgwas, although the Awgwas are visible to them. The immortals' friendship protects Claus: the Fairies rescue him from the mountain cave, and their Seals guard his dwelling.

records.l: toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The children's toys made by Claus bring happiness and encourage children to be obedient, reducing the Awgwas' influence over them. The Awgwas repeatedly steal the toys and store them in a lonely cavern, while Claus continues making more until his shelves are filled.

records.l: the Awgwas' wickedness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The Awgwas' wickedness includes inspiring angry passions, encouraging children to eat unripe fruit and disobey their parents, and taking pleasure in their suffering and punishment. They also attack Claus because his work limits their power over children.

records.l: the Awgwas' plot against Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The Awgwas' plot is to remove Claus from the children by abducting him, imprisoning him, stealing his toys, and blocking children from reaching him. Their attempts fail to destroy Claus, but they succeed for a time in keeping him from delivering his toys.

records.l: Claus's abduction, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The Awgwas first bind the sleeping Claus and carry him to a remote jungle in Ethop, where they leave him among dangerous animals. Later, they seize him while he travels to a village and imprison him in a mountain cave behind huge rocks.

records.l: Claus's escape, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 6. The Wickedness of the Awgwas
records.s: The Knooks rescue Claus from the jungle after he uses their secret sign and signal, then transport him home to the Laughing Valley. When the Awgwas imprison him in a mountain cave, the Fairies answer his mystic words and carry him back home.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: Ak confronts the Awgwas after they persecute Claus, but their King refuses to stop and declares that Claus will be killed within three days. Ak gathers the immortals, who prepare for war against the Awgwas and the evil creatures summoned to support them. In the battle at Laughing Valley, the immortals defeat the Awgwas, Dragons, Goblins, and most of the Giants, allowing Claus to carry his toys safely to children. Ak explains that the Awgwas have perished and that the powers of Good cannot be overthrown when opposed to Evil.

records.l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: Ak tells the Awgwas that Claus is under the protection of the immortals and orders them not to harm him. When the Awgwa King declares war and threatens to kill Claus, Ak organizes the immortals for battle, kills the King Awgwa with his ax, and later tells Claus that the Awgwas have perished.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: Claus is protected by the immortals after the Awgwas interfere with his work. While the battle is fought on his account, he remains in the Laughing Valley making toys, and afterward Ak tells him that he may carry them to children without fear.

records.l: Awgwas, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: The Awgwas refuse to stop persecuting Claus and defy Ak, claiming that their powers equal those of the immortals. They summon evil allies for war, but the immortals destroy them, turning them into earthen hillocks.

records.l: King Awgwa, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: The King Awgwa rejects Ak's demand to leave Claus unharmed and threatens to kill Claus within three days. He leads a large army against the immortals, but Ak cleaves him in two with his ax.

records.l: immortals, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: The immortals agree that the Awgwas must be destroyed because they devote themselves to evil and threaten Claus. They gather in the Laughing Valley and defeat the forces of evil before returning to their duties in the Forest.

records.l: war between the immortals and the spirits of evil, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: The war begins after the Awgwas refuse to obey Ak and threaten to kill Claus. The immortals fight the Awgwas and their allies in the Laughing Valley and win the battle.

records.l: spirits of evil, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: The spirits of evil are summoned by the King Awgwa to fight the immortals and include Asiatic Dragons, Tatary Giants, Black Demons, Goozzle-Goblins, and mountain Awgwas. Their forces are defeated, with only some of the Giants escaping.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: The Laughing Valley is where Claus makes his toys and where Ak orders the immortals to assemble for battle. The valley becomes the battlefield in which the immortals defeat the Awgwas and their allies.

records.l: toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: Claus continues making toys in the Laughing Valley while the immortals fight to protect him. After the Awgwas are destroyed, Ak tells Claus that he can carry the toys to dwellings and villages without fear.

records.l: Law, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: The Law states that Evil may accomplish terrible deeds when unopposed, but the powers of Good cannot be overthrown when opposed to Evil. The text says that the King Awgwa's ignorance of this Law costs him his existence.

records.l: Good, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: Good is represented by the immortals and their powers, which cannot be overthrown when they oppose Evil. The forces of Good defeat the Awgwas and their allies in the battle.

records.l: Evil, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 7. The Great Battle Between Good and Evil
records.s: Evil is represented by the Awgwas and the creatures they summon, whose actions are devoted to harm and misery. Evil is defeated when the immortals oppose it in battle.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Claus makes several journeys to distribute toys, then creates new dolls, animals, and musical instruments after studying children's tastes. During a deep winter, Flossie and Glossie visit him and help him build a sledge and harness so they can pull him to distant villages. On their first journey together, Claus travels by night, enters houses through chimneys, and leaves toys for sleeping children in a village and a large city. He empties his pack and barely returns to the Laughing Valley before daybreak, allowing the deer to reach the Forest before the Knooks' deadline.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Claus carries toys to children in hamlets, farmhouses, villages, and a large city, receiving grateful welcomes. He makes a sledge and harness, then rides with Flossie and Glossie on his first long journey with the reindeer, entering houses through chimneys to leave toys for sleeping children. He returns to the Laughing Valley just before daybreak.

records.l: Flossie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Flossie visits Claus with Glossie and explains that the snow is frozen hard enough for deer to walk on. She obtains permission from Will Knook to draw Claus on a journey, helps pull his sledge through the night, and urges Claus to hurry when dawn approaches.

records.l: Glossie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Glossie visits Claus with Flossie and explains that the Frost King has hardened the snow. He agrees to pull Claus's sledge after receiving permission from Will Knook, helps leap from roof to roof, and races back toward the Forest before daybreak.

records.l: Knooks, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: The Knooks are the guardians of Flossie and Glossie. Their permission is required for the deer to make the journey with Claus, and they would punish the deer if they failed to return to Burzee by daybreak.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: The Laughing Valley is Claus's home and workshop, where he stores and makes toys. Claus begins and ends his first journey with the reindeer there.

records.l: Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: The Forest is where Claus had known Flossie and Glossie, and where the deer normally live under the guardianship of the Knooks. The deer must return to the Forest by daybreak after their journey.

records.l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Children everywhere receive toys from Claus, including children who have never owned a toy. During the first journey with the reindeer, sleeping children in villages and a city receive dolls, drums, horns, elephants, and other playthings.

records.l: reindeer, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: The reindeer can walk easily across deep snow when its surface is frozen hard, and their fleet feet allow them to travel much faster than Claus can walk. Flossie and Glossie pull Claus and his pack on a sledge, leap between rooftops, and race home before dawn.

records.l: toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Claus makes and distributes dolls, animal figures, drums, cymbals, whistles, and horns. He leaves toys for sleeping children during his journeys until his supply is exhausted.

records.l: sledge, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Claus constructs a rude sledge from material in his wood-pile, using two upward-curving runners and short boards for a platform. He places a stool and his pack of toys on it, and Flossie and Glossie pull it swiftly over the snow and across rooftops.

records.l: harness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Claus makes a harness by twisting strong cords into collars for the deer and attaching other cords to the front of the sledge. He also uses cords fastened to the deer's antlers as reins, and later cuts the harness away so the deer can return to the Forest.

records.l: pack of toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Claus fills a pack with his prettiest toys and carries it on the sledge during the first journey with the reindeer. He empties the pack while visiting houses in a village and a large city.

records.l: snow, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: The Valley's snow lies many feet deep, but the Frost King freezes its surface so the deer can walk and the sledge can travel over it. The snow later supports the deer's rapid journey home, while Claus tumbles into a snowdrift when the sledge stops.

records.l: chimneys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Claus uses chimneys to enter houses whose doors are locked at night. He climbs down them to leave toys for sleeping children and climbs back up to return to the sledge.

records.l: villages, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: In a village Claus has never visited, he discovers that the locked doors prevent ordinary entry. With the deer's help, he reaches the rooftops, visits the houses through their chimneys, and leaves toys for every sleeping child.

records.l: the first journey with the reindeer, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: The first journey with the reindeer takes Claus, Flossie, and Glossie through the night to a village and a large city. Claus distributes his toys through chimneys and returns to the Laughing Valley just before daybreak, while the deer hurry back to the Forest.

records.l: colored toy-making, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 8. The First Journey with the Reindeer
records.s: Toy-making keeps Claus busy through the winter while deep snow prevents him from traveling. After observing children, he decides to make more dolls, animal figures, drums, cymbals, whistles, and horns.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 9. "Santa Claus!"
records.s: Claus's gifts become widely known, and people tell children stories about his wonderful toys. Parents explain that the toys came from the good Claus, whom mothers begin to regard as a Saint because of his mysterious ability to enter homes. Santa Claus brings toys because children are little and helpless and because he loves them, not because they are always well behaved. His good deeds cause people to enshrine him as a Saint in their hearts.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 9. "Santa Claus!"
records.s: Santa Claus becomes famous for giving wonderful toys to children. Mothers come to regard him as a Saint who can enter homes without unlocking doors, but he does not approve of using his gifts to threaten naughty children. He gives toys because children are little and helpless and because he loves them.

records.l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 9. "Santa Claus!"
records.s: Children find pretty toys by their bedsides and ask their parents where they came from. They are told that the good Claus brought them, and mothers teach them to pray to Santa Claus for forgiveness when they are naughty or disobedient. The text says that the best children are sometimes naughty and naughty children are often good.

records.l: toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 9. "Santa Claus!"
records.s: The toys Claus leaves by children's bedsides are described as pretty and wonderful. Parents say that they are the only toys in all the world made by the good Claus. Their appearance causes children and their parents to wonder how Claus entered the homes.

records.l: good deeds, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 9. "Santa Claus!"
records.s: Claus's generous work brings him fame that spreads into far lands, despite sneers from a few selfish people. His good deeds cause people to honor him as a Saint in their hearts.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Santa Claus asks Ak and other immortals to save Glossie and Flossie from punishment and secure permission for deer to draw his sledge on Christmas Eve. The Prince of the Knooks grants permission for up to ten deer to accompany Claus once a year, provided they return to the Forest by daybreak, and names them reindeer. Fairies recover the toys stolen by the Awgwas just before Christmas Eve, allowing Claus to make his first Christmas Eve journey and deliver gifts to children. He returns safely before daybreak, beginning a mission that brings happiness to hundreds of homes.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Santa Claus consults Ak after Will Knook threatens to punish Glossie and Flossie for returning one minute after daybreak. With the recovered toys, he makes his first Christmas Eve journey, delivering presents to children and returning home before daybreak.

records.l: Glossie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Glossie helps Claus on his night journey and returns one minute after daybreak, nearly receiving punishment from Will Knook. Glossie says the trip was enjoyable and later carries Claus swiftly home before daybreak on Christmas Eve.

records.l: Flossie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Flossie helps Claus on his night journey and returns one minute after daybreak, nearly receiving punishment from Will Knook. Flossie explains that they tried to get home by daybreak and later races with Glossie to return before dawn.

records.l: Will Knook, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Will Knook complains that Glossie and Flossie disobeyed his orders by staying out past daybreak and threatens to set stinging gnats on them. He objects to deer drawing Claus's sledge, but the Prince of the Knooks orders him to obey the granted permission.

records.l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Ak hears Claus's account and summons the Prince of the Knooks, the Fairy Queen, and the Prince of the Ryls to consider the deer’s punishment and service. He persuades the immortals to support Claus and calls Glossie and Flossie to confirm that they willingly drew the sledge.

records.l: Prince of the Knooks, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The Prince of the Knooks grants Claus permission to use up to ten deer once each year on Christmas Eve. He requires the deer to return to the Forest by daybreak and names those serving Claus reindeer, granting them additional protections and benefits.

records.l: Fairy Queen, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The Fairy Queen promises that no harm will come to the deer while they are away from the Forest. At Ak's request, she also tries to find the toys stolen by the Awgwas and sends Fairies to search for them.

records.l: Awgwas, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The Awgwas hid Claus's stolen toys in a deep cave in the mountains and covered the entrance with rocks. Their hiding place is eventually discovered and opened by the Fairies.

records.l: Knooks, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The Knooks guard the deer in the Forest and are described as unaccustomed to granting favors. Their Prince ultimately allows selected deer to serve Claus on Christmas Eve.

records.l: Fairies, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The Fairies search the mountains for the toys stolen by the Awgwas. By joining hands and moving through the rocks from the peak downward, they discover the cave, open it, carry out the toys, and bring them to Claus.

records.l: reindeer, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The reindeer are deer permitted to draw Claus's sledge on Christmas Eve, with up to ten allowed each year. They receive access to nourishing and strengthening plants, the Pool of Nares, and the Fairy Queen's protection, provided they return by daybreak.

records.l: Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The Forest is where the Knooks guard the deer and where Glossie and Flossie must return before daybreak. The deer serving Claus may bathe in its Pool of Nares.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The Laughing Valley is where Claus returns to work after consulting Ak. He leaves it with Glossie and Flossie at moonrise for his Christmas Eve journey and returns there after distributing the toys.

records.l: sledge, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Claus's sledge is drawn by Glossie and Flossie during his first Christmas Eve journey. Claus repairs its harness and strengthens it before loading it with toys and traveling south.

records.l: toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The Awgwas had stolen Claus's toys and hidden them in a cave beneath rocks in the mountains. The Fairies recover the toys just in time for Claus to load them onto his sledge and give them to children.

records.l: Christmas Eve, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Christmas Eve is established as the one night each year when Claus may use up to ten deer to draw his sledge. Claus's first journey on Christmas Eve takes him to farmhouses and a village, where he leaves toys for sleeping children.

records.l: Claus's first Christmas Eve journey, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Claus's first Christmas Eve journey begins after the Fairies recover the stolen toys. He travels with Glossie and Flossie, distributes gifts at farmhouses and in a village, empties his sack, and returns before daybreak.

records.l: recovery of the stolen toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: The recovery of the stolen toys occurs when the Fairies search through the mountain in a joined line and find the cave where the Awgwas hid them. They break open the cave and carry the toys to Claus shortly before Christmas Eve.

records.l: Santa Claus's mission to bring happiness to children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 10. Christmas Eve
records.s: Santa Claus's mission to bring happiness to children begins with his first Christmas Eve delivery of toys to sleeping children. The text says he has continued this mission for hundreds of years, bringing happiness to children's hearts.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: Santa Claus builds a larger sledge and prepares a team of ten reindeer so he can carry more toys to children on Christmas Eve. With help from the Gnome King and Peter Knook, he obtains steel runners, sleigh-bells, and strong leather harness materials. On one Christmas Eve, Margot, Dick, Ned, and Sara hang their wet stockings by the chimney, and Santa Claus fills them with toys. The children tell others, beginning the tradition of hanging stockings for Santa Claus, which helps him deliver presents more quickly.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: Santa Claus decides to spend the year making toys and to deliver them to children on Christmas Eve. He builds a larger sledge, obtains a harness for ten reindeer, and improves his toys with suggestions from the immortals. He fills the stockings of Margot, Dick, Ned, and Sara when he sees them hanging by the chimney.

records.l: reindeer (Claus's reindeer), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: Santa Claus's ten reindeer consist of Glossie, Flossie, Racer, Pacer, Reckless, Speckless, Fearless, Peerless, Ready, and Steady. They are selected for their likeness to Glossie and Flossie, strengthened with the casa plant, made fleet with the grawle plant, and given long lives through the marbon plant. They wear a new leather harness and pull Santa Claus's large sledge swiftly through the night.

records.l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: Children receive Santa Claus's toys and speak of him with love because of his unselfish deeds. Margot, Dick, Ned, and Sara discover toys in their stockings and tell their friends about it. Other children then decide to hang their stockings by the fireplace on Christmas Eve.

records.l: Santa Claus's new sledge, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: Santa Claus's new sledge is larger, stronger, and better suited for swift travel than his old one. It has curled steel runners from the Gnome King, a high rounded dashboard, high sides, and enough room for three full sacks of toys and additional toys in the sledge-box. The deer first consider it too large and heavy for two of them, so Santa Claus uses a team of ten.

records.l: toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: Santa Claus's toys become more beautiful and attractive as he works on them throughout the year. Some dolls say "papa" and "mama," lambs squeak, birds whistle, horses have wheels, and one donkey has a nodding head. On Christmas Eve, he loads three sacks and the rest of the sledge with toys for children.

records.l: the first stockings tradition, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: The first stockings tradition begins when Margot, Dick, Ned, and Sara's wet stockings are hung by the chimney to dry. Santa Claus notices them, fills them with toys, and inspires the children to tell others about what happened. The custom spreads, helping Santa Claus find children and deliver their presents more quickly.

records.l: Christmas Eve, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: On Christmas Eve, Santa Claus travels with his ten reindeer and a large load of toys to visit children around the world. The first stockings are hung by the chimney on this night, and Santa Claus fills them during his hurried visit. In later years, children hang stockings in anticipation of his arrival.

records.l: Santa Claus's Christmas-night journey, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: Santa Claus's Christmas-night journey takes him swiftly from chimney to chimney in his new sledge. He uses ten reindeer and sings as they travel over the frozen snow. After discovering the children's stockings, he realizes that filling them saves time compared with finding each child and placing toys beside the bed.

records.l: stockings (children's stockings), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 11. How the First Stockings Were Hung by the Chimneys
records.s: The children's stockings are hung in a row by the chimney so they can dry after Margot, Dick, Ned, and Sara play in the snow. Santa Claus sees them, stuffs toys into them, and leaves the children delighted the next morning. Their use spreads among other children as a convenient way for Santa Claus to deliver presents.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 12. The First Christmas Tree
records.s: Claus continues traveling around the world each Christmas Eve, bringing toys, fruit, candies, and other gifts to children. He discovers the idea of decorating a tree when he visits three neglected children living beneath a tent on a treeless plain. The children and their parents are filled with wonder, and Claus later carries Christmas trees to poor homes and decorates them with candles and toys. Years later, the new Baron Braun respectfully asks Claus to visit his children, and Claus agrees.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 12. The First Christmas Tree
records.s: Claus travels over the world on his sledge and returns to the Laughing Valley by daybreak. He brings children toys, fruit, candies, and decorated trees, and his kindness wins the hearts of everyone. He visits the children of the new Baron Braun after the Baron humbly asks him to do so.

records.l: reindeer (Claus's reindeer), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 12. The First Christmas Tree
records.s: Claus's ten reindeer carry him swiftly on his yearly trips around the world. Over eight years, each reindeer receives a string of bells from the Gnome King, so that all ten wear bells and make a merry tune as the sledge travels.

records.l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 12. The First Christmas Tree
records.s: Children receive toys, oranges, bananas, candies, and bonbons from Claus in their long stockings. They look forward to his yearly visit and gain happiness by wondering what will happen when he arrives. The children of the new Baron Braun long for a visit from Santa Claus, and Claus promises to bring them presents.

records.l: three little children (beneath the tent), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 12. The First Christmas Tree
records.s: The three little children live beneath a rude tent of skins on a broad treeless plain, and their parents sadly neglect them. Claus plants a pine tree near their tent, decorates it with candles, toys, and candies, and gives them their first great pleasure. They dance and laugh around the sparkling tree, while their parents begin to show them more respect and consideration.

records.l: pine tree (the tree Claus planted), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 12. The First Christmas Tree
records.s: Claus picks up the bushy top of a pine tree that the wind has broken off and carries it in his sledge. He plants it in the sand before the tent of the three little children and decorates its branches with candles and toys.

records.l: Christmas tree, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 12. The First Christmas Tree
records.s: The first Christmas tree in this account is made when Claus plants a pine tree for the three little children and decorates it with candles, toys, and candies. Pleased with the idea, Claus later carries trees to poor homes and decorates them for the children, while some fathers obtain trees for him to prepare.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: Santa Claus grows old and weak after many years of making and delivering toys to children, and the Forest of Burzee and Laughing Valley mourn his approaching death. Necile asks Ak for help, so he summons a council of the immortals to decide whether Claus deserves the Mantle of Immortality. Every immortal votes yes, and the Mantle is brought from its crypt and bestowed upon Claus. The Mantle becomes part of Claus's being, driving away the Spirit of Death and making him immortal.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: Santa Claus grows old, with white hair and beard, wrinkles, and a stout, waddling form, but he remains lively, jolly, and kind. After his strength is exhausted and he stops making toys, the immortals bestow the Mantle of Immortality upon him, making it part of his being.

records.l: Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: Necile, who reared Santa Claus as his foster mother, remains youthful, strong, and beautiful while he grows old. Troubled by the fate threatening Claus, she seeks Ak's help and later kisses Claus while admiring his immortal form.

records.l: Ak, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: Ak summons a council of the immortals after Necile tells him that Claus is near death. He argues that Claus deserves immortality and persuades the council to bestow the Mantle of Immortality upon him.

records.l: Spirit of Death, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: The Spirit of Death hovers near Santa Claus's bedside. When she sees the Mantle of Immortality, she retreats with disappointment and leaves the house forever.

records.l: Burzee, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: The Forest of Burzee becomes sad when Santa Claus grows old and appears near death. It later hosts the council where the rulers of the immortals gather to decide Claus's fate.

records.l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: The Laughing Valley is described as a peaceful place where Santa Claus has lived and maintained perfect health for many years. When he grows old and weak, the Valley is hushed and mournful.

records.l: immortals, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: The immortals gather in Burzee to consider Santa Claus's claim to immortality. Every immortal votes to give him the Mantle, and they carry it from its crypt and bestow it upon him.

records.l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: Children are the recipients of Santa Claus's toys and the beneficiaries of his lifelong work. Ak argues that Claus should live on because children would miss and grieve over his loss.

records.l: Mantle of Immortality, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: The Mantle of Immortality is a unique robe that has existed since the Beginning and is kept in a gleaming crypt between earth and sky. After every immortal votes for its use, it is placed upon Santa Claus, sinks into his body, and becomes a permanent part of his being.

records.l: council of the immortals, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: The council of the immortals is summoned by Ak in the Forest of Burzee to decide whether Santa Claus should receive the Mantle of Immortality. All members vote yes.

records.l: immortality, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: Immortality is presented as a gift reserved for one who truly deserves it, and no mortal had previously claimed the Mantle. Santa Claus receives immortality because of his noble nature and lifelong service to children.

records.l: Santa Claus's mission to bring happiness to children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, OLD AGE / 1. The Mantle of Immortality
records.s: Santa Claus's Christmas work consists of making toys and distributing them to children throughout the world. He performs this work for many years with the assistance and goodwill of the immortals, until old age finally prevents him from making more toys.

records.l: The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. When the World Grew Old
records.s: Santa Claus regains his youthful strength after winning the Mantle of Immortality through his love for little children. As the world’s population grows and spreads across the earth, Santa Claus expands his toy-making and gift-giving work with help from several immortals. Ak, the Knook Prince, the Ryl Prince, and the Fairy Queen each provide an assistant to help Santa Claus. Santa Claus’s reindeer carry him across land and sea so that he can visit children around the world each Christmas Eve.

records.l: Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus, 2. When the World Grew Old
records.s: Santa Claus awakens with his old strength renewed and feels as vigorous and merry as a boy of sixteen, although his beard remains white and wrinkles remain around his eyes. After learning about the Mantle of Immortality, he prepares more toys than ever and resolves that no child, poor or rich, should go without a Christmas gift if he can provide one. As the number of children grows, he receives help from Kilter, Peter, Nuter, and Wisk and continues his yearly work across the world.
